body:
### Summary

When `uv tool upgrade --all` encounters an error while enumerating the tool directory, it treats it as an empty tool set and reports `Nothing to upgrade`.

Reproduction:

```sh
tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
export UV_TOOL_DIR="$tmp"
mkdir "$UV_TOOL_DIR/tool backup"

uv tool list
echo "exit: $?"

uv tool upgrade --all
echo "exit: $?"
```

Observed output:

```text
error: Not a valid package or extra name: "tool backup". Names must start and end with
a letter or digit and may only contain -, _, ., and alphanumeric characters.
exit: 2
Nothing to upgrade
exit: 0
```
I expected `uv tool upgrade --all` to report the same invalid package-name error as `uv tool list` and exit nonzero.

I saw that the upgrade path uses:

```rust
installed_tools
    .tools()
    .unwrap_or_default()
```

With `.unwrap_or_default()`, an enumeration error becomes an empty collection. Would propagating the error instead with `?` be the intended behavior?


### Platform

Darwin 25.5.0 arm64

### Version

uv 0.12.3 (507230998 2026-08-07 aarch64-apple-darwin)

### Python version

Python 3.14.0
title: `uv tool upgrade --all` reports `Nothing to upgrade` when tool enumeration fails
